text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is weak evidence on its own. In bank risk functions it's statistically unremarkable, and tribunals and HR treat it as background, not proof. Leading with it invites the easy rebuttal that you're inferring bias from demographics alone.

Your stronger facts are concrete: on paper your credentials dominate his, and "broad experience of regulatory affairs" is vague enough to look reverse-engineered — though it may genuinely be what they wanted, since the role is regulator-facing.

So press the written reasons. Send a firm chase citing your original request date, ask for the scoring matrix and selection criteria. Panel composition becomes relevant only if those documents show subjective criteria applied inconsistently.
